title: /pick skill: rank the next ticket to pick up from the current repo's tracker
summary: A new shared skill, /pick, run from inside a repo. It reads the repo's issue_tracker from repo-policy.json (Linear for Quaestor-Web, GitHub for SpawnedSapien) and prints a ranked shortlist of tickets the user could start next. Each repo defines up to 4 named buckets (predefined native tracker queries) under a pick_buckets key. A bare /pick opens a bucket menu; free text after the command skips it. Shared-pool buckets also ask for a focus built from the user's current sprint projects. Fetch scripts normalize candidates, a Sonnet scoring agent (pick-scorer) ranks the top 25 by effort with a one-line reason each, and blocker tiers (ready, stackable, blocked) plus teammate-overlap rules shape the list. Output is terminal-only and read-only: top 5 plus up to 3 'other repos' tickets, each with a start line (wt <branch> [base] plus the ticket ID). The user then starts a new session and grills the ticket manually.
problem_statement: Choosing the next ticket costs 10 to 15 minutes of digging through queues, labels, and dependency chains. Three recurring cases: (a) in SpawnedSapien, picking from the GitHub issues queue by label priority (pre-launch before post-launch, opsec or polish by mood); (b) in Quaestor-Web, finding quick low-lift tickets from the Keystone Ready to Assign or Backlog pool when sprint scope runs low; (c) in Quaestor-Web, finding which follow-on tickets in the current sprint are not blocked while related PRs sit in review.
decisions: Skill name is /pick. Set disable-model-invocation: true so it only runs when the user types /pick.
The skill runs from inside a repo. It resolves the repo via the origin remote, looks up its repo-policy.json entry, and reads issue_tracker to choose the GitHub or Linear adapter.
Repos with no issue_tracker (dotfiles, ericlingren, or any repo not in policy) get a clean exit message, e.g. 'no issue_tracker configured for <repo>'. No fallback source.
The predefined queries are called buckets. Hierarchy: repo -> tracker (automatic) -> bucket -> tickets. Menu prompt is 'Which bucket?'.
Bucket definitions live in repo-policy.json under a pick_buckets key in each repo's entry. No separate config file.
Each bucket bundles its own filter (where to look) and sort. One click picks both.
Filter logic and sort logic (hide blocked, smallest first, label tier) are shared code. Bucket definitions are per-repo config.

Each bucket's filter uses the tracker's native query syntax: a GitHub search string for GitHub repos, a Linear IssueFilter JSON object for Linear repos. The script resolves 'me' to the user's Linear user id.
Max 4 buckets per repo, matching the 4-option menu limit. No paging. Other labels stay reachable through the free-text 'Other' option.
Lens selection: a bare /pick opens the bucket menu. Free text after /pick (e.g. '/pick quick wins') is mapped to a bucket and skips the menu.
User-facing wording says 'sprint', never 'cycle'. The Linear API's cycle terminology stays internal.

Quaestor-Web buckets: my-sprint (assignee is me, active cycle, state not completed or canceled; sort ready then stackable, smallest first; no focus menu) and unclaimed (team Keystone, unassigned, state in Ready to Assign or Backlog; sort smallest first; focus menu shown). No third bucket.
Keystone is a Linear team, not a project. The unclaimed filter uses the team key.

SpawnedSapien buckets: pre-launch ('is:open label:pre-launch -label:triage'), opsec ('is:open label:opsec,legal'), polish ('is:open label:polish -label:post-launch'), seed-ready ('is:open label:seed-ready').

Focus is asked each run, only for shared-pool buckets (e.g. unclaimed). Options are built live from projects in the user's own current sprint work, plus 'No focus' and free-text 'Other'. Focus is a ranking boost, not a filter. No stored or dated focus config.
Focus is not asked for my-sprint or for SpawnedSapien buckets, where the bucket choice already serves as focus.

Effort scoring: a cheap pre-sort on tracker fields narrows each bucket to the top 25. A dedicated Sonnet agent, pick-scorer, reads each candidate and scores effort with a rubric covering points, frontend vs backend, review complexity, target repo, and how clearly the ticket is scoped. Each result carries a one-line reason.
pick-scorer has a fixed JSON input/output contract so /improve-agent-benchmarks can tune it later.
In unclaimed, Ready to Assign (team-pointed) vs Backlog (unpointed) is a soft penalty, not a hard tier. Unpointed tickets carry a visible '⚠ unpointed' tag and can still rank high if clearly tiny.

Blocker tiers: ready (no blockers, or all blockers merged/Done) ranks first; stackable (every open blocker has a PR in review) ranks next and shows the blocker's branch as the base; blocked (any blocker not started or in progress with no PR) is hidden, with a count shown.
Blocker sources: Linear native blockedBy relations with blocker state and linked PRs; GitHub native issue dependencies plus 'blocked by #N' body text as fallback.
Teammate overlap at the parent/epic level (a teammate has active sibling tickets under the same parent) is hard-excluded.

Teammate overlap at the project level is a neutral annotation only (e.g. '👥 <name> active in <project>'). It does not affect rank, because the overlap can help (a reviewer with context) or hurt (ramp-up cost).
Tickets whose code lives in a different repo than the one /pick runs from are shown in a separate 'other repos' section below the main list, tagged with the target repo.
Output is a terminal list only. No picker UI, no auto-handoff into grill. The user starts a new session in a worktree and grills manually.

Each list item includes a copy-paste start line: 'wt <branch> [base]' plus the ticket ID. Stackable items pass the blocker's branch as the base. wt takes base as its second positional arg (no --base flag) and defaults to main.
Branch name in start lines: Linear gitBranchName for Linear tickets; a slug built from the issue title for GitHub issues.
Strictly read-only. No writes to Linear or GitHub: no assigning, no state moves, no labels, no estimate write-back.
Output is terminal-only. No report file is written.

All fetching runs through scripts in claude-code-shared/scripts/: pick-fetch-linear.sh (Linear GraphQL via LINEAR_API_KEY, same approach as fetch-linear-standup.sh) and pick-fetch-gh.sh (gh CLI). Both emit normalized candidate JSON.
Shortlist size: top 5 in the main section, up to 3 under 'other repos'.
/pick runs at a low tier as a thin orchestrator: menu, scripts, scorer agent, render.

Registration: pick in model-tiers.json; pick-scorer in agents/registry.json; skill-pipeline.json edge pick -> grill-me ('ticket chosen, start a new session and grill it'); standard learning-capture tail block with slug pick; add pick_buckets to whatever schema the repo-policy validator checks.
implementation_decisions: Example pick_buckets entry shape: { "<bucket-name>": { "where": <native query>, "sort": ["hide-blocked", "smallest"] } }, keyed under the repo's existing repo-policy.json entry.
Linear my-sprint filter: {"cycle":{"isActive":{"eq":true}},"assignee":{"isMe":{"eq":true}}} plus a state filter excluding completed and canceled.
Example list item: '1. ✅ QW-1482  <title>  ~1pt  FE' / 'why: <one-line reason>' / '👥 <name> active in <project>' / 'start: wt <branch> [base]  ->  /grill-me QW-1482'.
Menu headers show the active focus when one is chosen.
Free-text after /pick maps to a bucket name; it is plain English, not a flag.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Linear workflow state names 'Ready to Assign' and 'Backlog' and the Keystone team key were not verified against the API in session. The build should verify them with one read-only GraphQL query.
disable-model-invocation: true was stated as supported in skill frontmatter but was not verified against Claude Code docs in session.
tests/test-standup-registration.sh validates the repo-policy schema. If it rejects unknown keys, pick_buckets must be added to the checked schema.
LLM effort estimates may be unreliable at first. The fixed pick-scorer contract allows tuning via /improve-agent-benchmarks; a code-peek scoring mode was considered and left for later.
grill-me fetches Linear IDs only. A GitHub start line like '/grill-me #205' will not auto-fetch the issue; the user accepted this since they start the grill manually.

The conversation did not settle whether blocker tiers apply to unclaimed and the SpawnedSapien buckets, or only to my-sprint. The SpawnedSapien pre-launch bucket was drafted with hide-blocked; unclaimed was drafted with smallest-first only.
